validated_results.title: Boron intake and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Prospective VITAL cohort analysis reporting hazard ratios for boron intake and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake (diet plus multivitamins)
extraction.population: Men who completed the baseline supplement and food frequency questionnaire in the VITamins And Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort

sample_size.excerpt: We evaluated the association between boron intake and prostate cancer within the VITamins And Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort. A total of 35,244 men completed the baseline supplement and food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) in 2000-2002.

cases.excerpt: A total of 832 men developed prostate cancer from baseline to 31 December 2004.

effect_size.excerpt: The hazard ratio of prostate cancer for those in the highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake was 1.17 (95% CI 0.85, 1.61). This risk did not vary by prostate cancer stage or Gleason score.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The hazard ratio of prostate cancer for those in the highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake was 1.17 (95% CI 0.85, 1.61).

comparison.excerpt: for those in the highest versus lowest quartile of total boron intake

design.excerpt: This cohort study provides no evidence for a preventive role of boron intake on prostate cancer.

timing.excerpt: A total of 832 men developed prostate cancer from baseline to 31 December 2004.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A boron database was constructed from published sources to estimate boron intake from the FFQ and from multivitamins.
